recommendation_summary: Replace the row and object materialization with a PostgreSQL COUNT(*) that keeps the existing unpaid filter, inside the current application and database. Add an index only if the query plan supports it, and verify end-to-end latency under representative load before claiming the one-second target. No new services or topics are added. The reply rejects an asynchronous projection because it could lag committed invoices. No unmet needs remain, though latency is not yet proven.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You require a count within one second that reflects committed invoices at request time; you proposed CQRS and Redis.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, CQRS projection, and Redis for this count. Approved budget and peer adoption do not establish a need.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint retrieves and constructs rows solely to count them; database query cost remains unknown.
labels.Checked myself: Only the supplied behavior and requirements; no query plan or timing evidence.

note: The reply picks a bounded aggregate query, rejects the Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack by name, keeps request-time freshness, and makes no claims of inspection it could not have done.
